newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 52-week T-bill yield seen stable or just up.
newsitem.headline: Polish 52-week T-bill yield seen stable or just up.

text.p: Polish 52-week T-bill yields are expected to hold steady or inch up at Thursday's 500 million zloty primary tender but foreign investor demand is likely to be capped by the surging zloty, dealers said on Wednesday.

They said that yields may be topping out after growing for the last several months, with some expecting yields to inch up another several basis points on Thursday and others seeing yields hovering around Monday's average yield of 21.87 percent.

"Yields are likely to remain basically flat on Thursday, with the average yield perhaps moving closer toward Monday's maximum of 21.93 percent," said Wojciech Labryga, T-bill dealer from Bank Slaski SA.
But others said yields could rise further as the zloty, trading at a six-week high against the basket of currencies on Wednesday, would deter yield-depressing foreign investor entry.
"The strong zloty will cut foreign demand and the maximum yield could rise to around 22.00 percent," said Piotr Korcz, T-bill dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
But some dealers said several foreign investors had already exchanged currencies for zlotys ahead of Thursday's auction guarding against further zloty gains tomorrow or on Friday.
Dealers said the Treasury offered an additional tender on Thursday because it wanted to absorb the 500 million zlotys of rejected 52-week T-bill bids at Monday's weekly auction.
They said that even though Polish yields may be reaching a ceiling they were unlikely to go down for some time.
"Yields are on a hilltop right now but it seems like the top is a plateau with no significant cuts expected amid high money market rates," said Marcin Dec from Bank Gdanski SA.

The zloty closed on Wednesday at 3.25/3.20 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 3.17/3.13 percent, with the central bank reluctant to restrain the rise through currency-buying intervention ahead of the T-bill tender.
It closed at 3.1080/00 to the dollar, down from 3.1070/80 on Tuesday and at 1.8085/00 to the mark, up from 1.8120/30.
